diagrams.title: Choose the Offer, Build Trust, Earn the Referral
diagrams.subtitle: Match recurring economics to buyer intent before introducing the affiliate offer.
diagrams.caption: Michael Bashi favors recurring software commissions; Adam Enfroy connects search demand, commissions, and competitive weaknesses; Brian Brewer demonstrates capture and introduction.
diagrams.assumptions_note: This sequence combines Michael Bashi, Adam Enfroy, Smart Capital, Brian Brewer, and Cesar O. Vlogs. It is not a single campaign with a shared earnings result or completion deadline.
diagrams.note: Cesar O. Vlogs reports a year to their first commission. Smart Capital emphasizes retention, attribution windows, and refund terms rather than the headline commission alone.

stages.label: Match a buyer problem
stages.detail: Adam Enfroy looks for the intersection of search demand, good commissions, and weaknesses that better content can address.

stages.label: Inspect recurring economics
stages.detail: Michael Bashi favors useful subscription software with recurring monthly affiliate payments.

stages.label: Check retention and terms
stages.detail: Smart Capital compares customer retention and checks cookie windows and refunds before counting earnings.

stages.label: Capture and introduce
stages.detail: Brian Brewer demonstrates lead capture, a personal introduction, and automated selling around an audience-aligned offer.

stages.label: Nurture with useful email
stages.detail: Cesar O. Vlogs includes value-only emails without links rather than making every message a promotion.

diagrams.title: AI Visibility Is Not a Customer Conversion Rate
diagrams.subtitle: Keep prompt coverage, citations, observation time, engine coverage, and qualified demos distinct.
diagrams.caption: E-commerce Berlin Expo reports a citation experiment; TOP Digital Products describes engine coverage; Rob Hoffman reports qualified demos from comparison pages.
diagrams.assumptions_note: E-commerce Berlin Expo, TOP Digital Products, and Rob Hoffman describe different measurements and operations. These are independent checkpoints, not a decreasing cohort funnel; no stage-to-stage conversion rate is established.
diagrams.note: The E-commerce Berlin Expo presenters continued testing citation durability. Rob Hoffman's roughly ten weekly qualified demos must not be attributed to their citation test or to the tool covered by TOP Digital Products.

stages.label: Tracked prompt panel
stages.detail: E-commerce Berlin Expo describes a panel of 143 prompts for the external-source citation experiment.

stages.label: External-source citations
stages.detail: E-commerce Berlin Expo reports approximately 800 citations after placing content on a domain not previously used as a source for the panel.

stages.label: Initial observation interval
stages.detail: E-commerce Berlin Expo reports the initial citation result after five days, with durability still under examination.

stages.label: AI engine coverage
stages.detail: TOP Digital Products describes ZeroRank visibility tracking across seventeen AI engines.

stages.label: Qualified demo outcome
stages.detail: Rob Hoffman reports this weekly result for Team Town comparison pages and says the team uses GA4 to track performance.

diagrams.title: Entry Revenue and Spend Without a False Profit Total
diagrams.subtitle: Separate Jay Neyer's annual paid-experience results from Jamie McAdam's daily low-ticket test.
diagrams.caption: Jay Neyer reports birthday-booking and play-pass revenue; Jamie McAdam recalls daily entry-funnel sales and advertising spend from a separate test.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Jay Neyer's annual figures and Jamie McAdam's daily figures are independent reported amounts. Every bar is a standalone total, not a cumulative waterfall adjustment. The combined paid-experience figure overlaps the component categories.
diagrams.note: Jay Neyer's 'over' amounts retain their reported thresholds. Jamie McAdam's daily sales range does not establish high-ticket purchases, complete operating costs, or net profit.

diagrams.title: Read the Clock Behind the Commission
diagrams.subtitle: Attribution windows, withdrawal timing, and recurring commission duration are different terms.
diagrams.caption: Kris the Entrepreneur describes cookie windows; Khris Steven describes withdrawal timing; Adam Enfroy checks recurring commission cutoffs.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Kris the Entrepreneur, Khris Steven, and Adam Enfroy provide examples rather than a market-wide timing distribution. Units remain explicit on each bar. The typical field uses a reported value or range endpoint, not an estimated average.
diagrams.note: Khris Steven's two-to-five-business-day withdrawal statement is not a cookie window. Adam Enfroy's twelve-month cutoff check is not a promise of lifetime commissions.
diagrams.unit: Reported duration; days, business days, or months as labeled

bars.label: Recurring cutoff to inspect
bars.display: 12 months — Adam Enfroy checks beyond this cutoff

diagrams.title: Publish for the Buyer's Decision
diagrams.subtitle: Require genuine product fit, matching search intent, the right next action, and checked facts.
diagrams.caption: Alex COLLINSEO, ToolTester Pro, Affiliate Marketing How To, and The SEO Desk supply the publication checks.
diagrams.assumptions_note: These gates combine Alex COLLINSEO's fit test, ToolTester Pro's search inspection, Affiliate Marketing How To's intent-specific actions, and The SEO Desk's fact checks. Passing them does not guarantee rankings or sales.
diagrams.note: The Grow and Convert Marketing Show defines its reported alternative-content conversions as product-related actions such as trial starts or demo requests, not newsletter signups.

nodes.question: Does the proposed alternative genuinely fit the searcher's request?
nodes.fail_action: Pass on the stretched comparison, as Alex COLLINSEO recommends, rather than assuming ranking creates sales.

nodes.question: Do the live search results support the intended answer format and buyer decision?
nodes.fail_action: Follow ToolTester Pro by inspecting the winning page's first screen, structure, and answer format, then searching the same term.

nodes.question: Does the next action match this intent group?
nodes.fail_action: Follow Affiliate Marketing How To by separating affiliate-program invitations from pricing and trial offers.

nodes.question: Have changing prices, features, and other vulnerable facts actually been checked?
nodes.pass_next: Publish with a real last-check date
nodes.fail_action: Follow The SEO Desk by keeping a short list of vulnerable facts and verifying them before assigning a last-check date.

diagrams.title: Build Newsletter Growth Around Reader Value
diagrams.subtitle: Connect editorial quality, acquisition, onboarding, and monetization without mistaking subscriber totals for value.
diagrams.caption: Josh Spector, Matt McGarry, Marketing Max, Louis Nicholls, and Ryan Sneddon describe complementary newsletter functions in SparkLoop interviews.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The functions synthesize SparkLoop interviews with different operators, including Josh Spector and Matt McGarry. They do not describe one employer's organization or establish staffing requirements.
diagrams.note: Matt McGarry recommends approximately thirty days of paid-source engagement assessment. Wanda Zelaya reports rejection from paid recommendations, so access must not be treated as automatic.

center.focus: Josh Spector emphasizes specific value for a specific audience; SparkLoop's subscriber-value discussion begins with identifying a good reader and their economic value.

spokes.type: Operating function, not a staffing count
spokes.kpi: Ryan Sneddon's final checks cover dates, weekdays, venues, and source websites.

spokes.type: Operating function, not a staffing count
spokes.kpi: Office Party reports $0.50–$1.50 per subscriber after testing; Matt McGarry examines downstream engagement by source over approximately thirty days.

spokes.type: Operating function, not a staffing count
spokes.kpi: Marketing Max reports landing-page conversion moving from 7% to 35%; SparkLoop recommends source-specific welcome messages that repeat the reader benefits.

spokes.type: Operating function, not a staffing count
spokes.kpi: Louis Nicholls emphasizes signup and early-email monetization; Josh Spector reports five-to-ten-times more clicks from outcome-led sponsorship placements.

diagrams.title: Keep Borrowed-Authority Measurements Separate
diagrams.subtitle: Keyword positions, citation counts, referral visitors, and guide reductions answer different questions.
diagrams.caption: Edward Sturm reports keyword contraction; CrowdReply reports citations; Spencer on Niche Pursuits Podcast reports referral traffic; Ahrefs describes Brian Powell's guide reduction.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Edward Sturm, CrowdReply, Niche Pursuits Podcast, and Ahrefs describe independent cases. Low and high retain reported endpoints, conflicting spoken counts, or subset-and-total counts as explained per bucket; they are not additive allocations or statistical confidence intervals.
diagrams.note: Rankso SEO separates discussion visibility, contribution visibility, destination visits, and useful customer actions. SERPSUPPORT warns that rented rankings can be taken away.
diagrams.total_range: No combined total — independent keyword, citation, visitor, and guide counts

buckets.label: Top-three keyword contraction
buckets.notes: Edward Sturm reports around 10,400 high-volume top-three keywords falling to 3,300 in one month. The endpoints describe a decline, not a forecast.

buckets.label: Spoken citation counts
buckets.notes: CrowdReply states 230 citations across five prompts and six AI models at the cited moment, then says 213 later. These are differing spoken figures, not a measured uncertainty interval.

buckets.label: Reddit subset and site total
buckets.notes: Spencer on Niche Pursuits Podcast reports nearly 10,000 Reddit visitors within 16,000 total visitors over approximately 28 days. The lower endpoint retains the rounded 'nearly' figure; the two counts overlap and must not be added.

buckets.label: Affiliate guides removed
buckets.notes: Ahrefs describes Brian Powell cutting about 25 guides while maintaining important pages. This is a portfolio reduction count, not a traffic total.

diagrams.title: Make the Relationship Clear and the Claims Supportable
diagrams.subtitle: Sequence disclosure placement, presentation checks, claim evidence, and brand-name advertising inspection.
diagrams.caption: Erika Kullberg, Michael Ostheimer, Carmen, Cohen at AM Days, Gordon at Venable LLP, Analytics Playbook, and Grow My Ads provide the readiness checks.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The weekly slots organize checks described by Erika Kullberg, Michael Ostheimer, AM Days, Venable LLP, Analytics Playbook, and Grow My Ads. They are planning slots, not practitioner claims about task duration or a grace period for disclosure.
diagrams.note: Michael Ostheimer says disclosures must work on smartphones and match visual or audible claims. Carmen says account-level disclosure does not replace disclosure on individual posts.

weeks.title: Place relationship explanations
weeks.deliverable: Put commission language beside affiliate links, as Erika Kullberg demonstrates. Michael Ostheimer identifies 'paid link' as a compact option; Carmen also discloses on individual affiliate posts.
weeks.gate: The connection is visible beside the recommendation, not left solely to an account-level statement.

weeks.title: Check mobile and media presentation
weeks.deliverable: Inspect the smartphone presentation and match visual and audible disclosures to the endorsement, following Michael Ostheimer. Identify each free-product connection as Erika Kullberg recommends.
weeks.gate: The disclosure remains clear on the phone and in the relevant visual or audio presentation.

weeks.title: Substantiate product and earnings claims
weeks.deliverable: Check testimonials, before-and-after images, and product claims against supporting evidence, following Cohen at AM Days. Apply Gordon's Venable LLP warning about earnings-result tracking and easy-money claims.
weeks.gate: Do not rely on advertiser copy as proof; remove claims that everyone makes money or that the process is easy.

weeks.title: Inspect visible brand-name advertising
weeks.deliverable: Follow Analytics Playbook by avoiding dynamic keyword insertion and disabling automatically created assets in competitor campaigns. Inspect dynamic search advertising for the name-insertion problem reported by Grow My Ads.
weeks.gate: Inspect actual visible copy for unintended competitor names rather than assuming keyword selection and published wording are the same.
